purpose: Teach: 洋楽/紅白/表参道/ビーズ/格言/コンテナ/ワゴン/エサ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが洋楽レコードを集められたぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father was young — he used to collect Western records.
lines.style: Soft, distant voice reaching backward through decades. Gentle opening on 'You know.' Slow measured pace. Slight pause before the memory lands. Warm but tinged with the particular sadness of remembering someone no longer here.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、紅白歌合戦を毎年楽しみにされてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, he did — and your grandfather loved watching the Kohaku Uta Gassen every single year, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm, affectionate, meeting him in the memory. Gentle tilt upward at the end — not a question, but an invitation. Familiar cadence of long partnership. Voice settled and sure.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが表参道を歩かれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, he used to walk down Omotesando all the time.
lines.style: Eyes distant again. Opening slower than the last line. Voice grows quieter reaching the place name — as if saying it aloud brings the street back. Small pause at the end, like he's standing there again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ばあさんにビーズの首飾りを贈ってくださったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather gave me such a beautiful beaded necklace, didn't he, dear? I still remember that.
lines.style: Tender recognition, the warmth of a specific touch remembered. Voice lifts slightly on the necklace — it mattered, it still matters. Slow, savoring the detail. Gentle confirmation at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは格言をよく口にされてたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, he was always quoting sayings. Always had one on his lips.
lines.style: Quieter this time. Voice takes on a reflective quality, almost like he's hearing those sayings again. Deliberate pace. The warmth of recognizing someone's particular way of speaking.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、貨物コンテナを使う仕事をされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather worked with shipping containers, didn't he? Such hard work.
lines.style: Gentle acknowledgment of labor and care. Voice steady and grounded. Small warmth on 'such hard work' — recognizing the effort it took. Close and intimate, bridging their separate memories into one.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、屋台のワゴンでうどんを食べたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, we'd eat udon from those street food carts.
lines.style: Voice warming slightly, the memory more tactile now — taste, steam, the casual contentment of simple food shared. Slower, savoring the ordinary moment held in time. Slight nostalgic lift at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、鳥にエサをあげるのお好きだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather loved feeding the birds, didn't he? Such a gentle thing he'd do.
lines.style: Voice very close now, intimate and sure. Slow, tender delivery. The recognition of a small kindness that was deeply him. Soft fadeout at the end — like a hand settling.
